item.description:

The rest of it talks about how buses are packed as people shift to public transit, bus commutes are much faster, and bus companies are adding buses to increase supply. This is a clear victory for efficiency. Maybe he’s just being “Straussian” in his dogged opposition to this improvement.

item.title: Comment on Do Migrants Pay Their Way? A Net Fiscal Analysis for Germany by I do wonder how they define migrant
item.description:
First, Asylanten are not considered officially migrants, though their status can change.

Second in the region where I live, a lot of German citizens live in France and work in Germany, while a number of French citizens work in German companies on this side of the Rhine. A similar effect involving the Netherlands can be found in the region around Venlo/Nettetal or around Aachen. Then there is Basel, with Switzerland, Germany, and France basically sharing a regional area, where a French citizen living in Germany can be working for a company in Switzerland.

Third, do seasonal agricultural workers from countries such as Romania count as migrants?

In other words, and without going into further details, I have some serious doubts this paper says much of anything concerning 'migrants' that is useful.
